text:
sophia: FYI I'm seeing a reproducible TP all-reduce tail on the 8xA100 fleet for long context runs. Sequence length 2048, batch per device 1. Ring path latency jumps around 30-60ms per step for some ranks, tree fallback cuts variability but higher median. Dumped NCCL topo + kernel selector logs.

liam: ugh. is this only on ring or also when we force tree? numbers?

sophia: ring: median 18ms, p95 62ms, p99 120ms. tree: median 26ms, p95 48ms, p99 72ms. So tree reduces p99 but hurts median. Behavior correlated with message sizes ~56-80KB (post-chunking).

arjun: can you paste the kernel selector output? maybe autoswitch is picking a slow kernel for that msgsize regime.

sophia: pasted logs below. the selector picks kernel v2_smallfrag for chunk_size 4k which increases fragmentation across the ring.

```
[2026-03-18T12:03:01Z] selector: model=redwood-13b, seq=2048, kvcache=true
chosen_kernel=v2_smallfrag
est_io_per_step=72KB
notes=frag_count=14,kv_shard=8
```

liam: that frag_count is suspicious. our ring RPCs blow up with many small fragments because handshakes/pack overheads dominate. we should try aligning chunk boundaries to 128KB and see if kernel autoswitch moves to v2_regular.

tess: quick experiment: forced kernel=v2_regular + chunk_align=128KB on a staging 8-GPU run yields: ring median 20ms, p95 34ms, p99 56ms. not as good as pure tree p99 but much nicer median and fewer outliers.

mike: did you try enabling comm/compute overlap? our pipeline allows overlap if reduce ops are async and kv flushes are delayed.

tess: yes, overlap on: ring median 17ms, p95 30ms, p99 58ms. So overlap helps median but p99 still high when frag_count > 10.

arjun: hypothesis: small fragment handoffs create variable enqueue latency across ranks (NIC contention + kernel queuing). Patch idea: add smallfrag coalesce window (5ms) before issuing NCCL op to aggregate adjacent fragments into bigger messages. tradeoff: added latency for small cases but should lower p99 for long sequences.

sophia: can we reproduce the NIC enqueue variance? I dumped per-rank tx queue lengths and see spikes aligned with epoch boundaries. pasted snippet:

```
rank 0 txq=12 spike@12:04:11
rank 1 txq=3
rank 2 txq=14 spike@12:04:11
rank 3 txq=11
rank 4 txq=2
rank 5 txq=13 spike@12:04:11
rank 6 txq=1
rank 7 txq=10
```

liam: looks like a synchronized pattern — warmup/kvcache flush maybe causing bursts. are we scheduling KV cache flushes at the same microstep across TP ranks?

sophia: yes by default we flush at layer boundaries. seems TP pipeline timing makes multiple ranks flush simultaneously.

mike: two actionable things: 1) try staggering kvcache flush offset per rank (config param flush_jitter_ms=rank_id*1ms) 2) implement coalesce window for small fragments in runtime. both low-risk.

tess: I ran jitter=1ms per rank + chunk_align=128KB + kernel=v2_regular on staging. results: ring median 16ms, p95 28ms, p99 34ms. p99 collapsed — looks promising.

arjun: great. we should still add a perf regression test: create a microbench with seq_len sweep [512,1024,1536,2048], chunk_align toggles, flush_jitter toggle, and kernel selector deterministic seeding to avoid flapping. capture NCCL timelines and per-rank enqueue histograms.

sophia: I'll open a PR with the microbench and a patch for flush_jitter config. also filing a perf alert for prod with the new thresholds.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1173 — TP all-reduce tail; assignees: @sophia @arjun; priority: P2

liam: thanks. after PR, let's run canary on Dedicated for a few hours with seq=2048 and monitor console dashboards (per-token latency + nccl p99).

sophia: plan: PR by EOD, canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC, rollback plan is to revert kernel override and disable jitter.

mike: quick note for docs: add guidance to Optimize -> batching heuristics about chunk_align and flush_jitter for TP workloads. small doc snippet in PR would help customers replicate fixes.

sophia: agreed. I'll include it. Closing loop once canary finishes. :thumbsup:
